name: Smart Autocorrect

releases.author: Zangeti
releases.description: Semantic inline link underlining (experimental) built on the LSTM embedding matching; a real personal-dictionary editor (added-by-you vs learned); 'i'->'I'; and a Convenience settings group with euro placement, negative amounts, ISO currency codes, and fraction glyphs.

releases.author: Zangeti
releases.description: Currency popup polish (no 💱, suppress all currency words after a number) and removal of the brittle retroactive-casing rewrite. Forward casing in suggestions is unchanged.

releases.author: Zangeti
releases.description:
### Currency
- Symbols now sit where each currency actually goes: signs like \$ € ¥ ₹ lead the number, while the dong, krona, złoty, franc, hryvnia and ruble trail it ("1,000 ₫").
- Decimals are padded to at least two places ("10.5" → "10.50"), and a 3-digit decimal is no longer misread as a thousands group.
- The popup offers a single "Format currency" action (with the target symbol on the right), not a reformatted string or a "dollars" completion. It fires for "\$10000", "10000\$", "1000euro" and partial words, and Tab applies the whole conversion at once.
- Undoing a currency or ordinal fix no longer adds the token to your dictionary.

### Casing
- Proper nouns keep their capital: "Federal " suggests "Reserve", and "federal Reserve" is repaired to "Federal Reserve".

### Tags
- The tag popup shows up to five matching existing tags first, then a few new ones.

releases.author: Zangeti
releases.description:
### Currency
- Symbols now sit where each currency conventionally goes ($100, €100, but 100 kr).
- The number to convert no longer spans a space, so "2003 34 dollars" becomes "2003 $34".
- Works without a trailing space ("1000euro"), and is offered in the suggestion popup with the symbol shown, so Tab does the whole transform at once.
- Decimal mark is kept as you typed it (with "none") or set by the thousands separator.
- Currency options moved to their own "Additional features" settings group.

### Predictions & autocorrect
- Sharper "Suggest alternatives": a short list of genuinely close synonyms instead of a padded menu.
- Numeric tidying: 21th → 21st, 1930's → 1930s.
- Proper-noun casing repaired in phrases ("federal Reserve" → "Federal Reserve").
- "2$ " now offers a following-word suggestion.
- Within-document cache boost is bounded, so a rare note word can't take over the menu.

### Layout
- Writing stats and the support block sit together, below the reset buttons.
- Tag suggestions show your matching existing tags first, then a few new ones.

releases.author: Zangeti
releases.description:
### ✨ Highlights

**Suggest alternatives is now context-aware.** Right-click a word and the ranking uses the sentence around it — "the coffee was very **strong**" → *potent / intense*, not *weak*. Built on the lexical-substitution literature (substitutability × context fit), with a learned valence direction that pushes antonyms down and an oracle filter that drops junk and misspellings.

**New: automatic currency tidying.** Type the number and it formats — `$1000` → `$1,000`, `1000 euros` → `€1,000`. Covers all major world currencies; the thousands separator (comma / period / none) is a setting. On by default.

### Also in this release
- More aggressive autocorrect for clear non-words (real-word overrides stay conservative).
- Writing stats moved to the top of settings.
- The "yours" badge / personal dictionary only holds words nothing else recognises; stale entries are tidied automatically.
- Tag suggestions accept with Tab and close on accept.
- The alternatives menu is now an inline popup at the word (Tab to accept, more than three options).
- Fixes the "odd suggestion after a while, gone after reload" drift, and reads the live editor buffer for tag/dictionary sync.

releases.author: Zangeti
releases.description: ✨ **New: Suggest alternatives.** Right-click (or highlight) a word and pick a more eloquent, academic alternative — `good` → substantial / exemplary, `help` → facilitate, `big` → immense. It's drawn entirely from the on-device model, so it works offline like everything else. Toggle it in settings (on by default), and there's a new "Word alternatives used" stat.
releases.name: Smart Autocorrect 1.0.6

releases.author: Zangeti
releases.description:
Wording, settings, and consistency polish.

- **Cleaner settings**: advanced sections now collapse into their own sub-pages (or fold-away sections on older Obsidian), so the main settings screen isn't a wall of options.
- **Friendlier copy**: the getting-started tour and settings descriptions are simpler and more natural, and the "undo" step now just says what it does — press undo and your word comes back.
- **Respects your capitalisation**: a word you typed as "Nasdaq" stays "Nasdaq" — it won't be overruled to "NASDAQ". The popup and autocorrect no longer disagree about casing.
- **Sensible dictionary rules**: a word that's already recommendable isn't offered for "add to dictionary", and a real word the model doesn't happen to know is never "corrected" away.
- **Tidier personal dictionary**: words are removed more reliably once they no longer appear anywhere in your vault.
releases.name: Smart Autocorrect 1.0.5

releases.author: Zangeti
releases.description:
Bug-fix release.

- **Numbers**: ordinals and units like `19th`, `3rd`, `1/16th`, `5km` are no longer "corrected".
- **Brackets**: accepting a completion right after `(` no longer inserts a stray space.
- **Acronyms**: plural acronyms (`CMOs`, `URLs`) are left alone; undoing a correction now pins the exact spelling/casing (e.g. `Nasdaq`) so it stops being re-cased.
- **Contractions**: suggestions like `Roosevelt's` and `didn't` no longer show up as `Roosevelt s` / `didn t`.
- **More suggestions**: a sparse menu is topped up from the bundled word list.
- **Tags**: a `#tag` is only mirrored into frontmatter once you've finished typing it.
- **Download dialog**: shorter and friendlier.
- **Stability**: fixes odd out-of-context recommendations that used to creep in after a long typing session (and cleared only on reload) — the within-document cache now stays in sync with the note as you edit.
releases.name: Smart Autocorrect 1.0.4

releases.author: Zangeti
releases.description:
Housekeeping from the plugin review. No user-facing changes.

The 1.13-only settings API is now reached only where it exists, so the plugin still supports Obsidian 1.11.4 and up.

The language model files are unchanged and stay on the [1.0.0 release](https://github.com/Zangeti/obsidian-smart-autocorrect/releases/tag/1.0.0); the plugin downloads them from there on first run.
releases.name: Smart Autocorrect 1.0.3

releases.author: Zangeti
releases.description:
Adopts Obsidian's declarative settings API, so every setting is findable from settings search on 1.13.0 and later. The pane itself is unchanged, and still works the same way on older versions.

The language model files are unchanged and stay on the [1.0.0 release](https://github.com/Zangeti/obsidian-smart-autocorrect/releases/tag/1.0.0); the plugin downloads them from there on first run.
releases.name: Smart Autocorrect 1.0.2

releases.author: Zangeti
releases.description:
Fixes raised by the Obsidian plugin review. No user-facing behaviour changes.

- The plugin is no longer used as the component for markdown previews, so nothing a preview registers outlives the preview.
- Timers and element creation use `window.*` and Obsidian's `createEl` helpers, so the UI behaves in popout windows.
- The `[[` picker is docked from code rather than a stylesheet, removing a `:has()` selector and its `!important` overrides.
- LICENSE is plain MIT again (the Various Complements attribution is now in NOTICE).
- Release assets are built and attested in CI.

The language model files are unchanged and stay on the [1.0.0 release](https://github.com/Zangeti/obsidian-smart-autocorrect/releases/tag/1.0.0); the plugin downloads them from there on first run.
releases.name: Smart Autocorrect 1.0.1

releases.author: Zangeti
releases.description:
First release.

**Installing manually:** put `main.js`, `manifest.json` and `styles.css` in `<vault>/.obsidian/plugins/smart-autocorrect/`, then enable the plugin. It will offer to download the language model on first run.

The three `.bin` files are the language model (86 MB total). The plugin fetches them from this release automatically, so you do not normally need to download them by hand. They are verified against these checksums:
